answer.reason: The verses tell of Shebna's part in the Assyrian envoy's demand at Jerusalem and of his being sent to Isaiah, which adds deeds beyond the summary.

clauses.english: asked Rabshakeh to speak in the Syrian language, not the Jews' language, in the hearing of the people on the wall
clauses.quote: Speak, I pray thee, to thy servants in the Syrian language

clauses.english: was sent in sackcloth by Hezekiah to Isaiah the prophet
clauses.quote: And he sent Eliakim, which was over the household, and Shebna the scribe,

doubts: ISA 22:15 names a Shebna the treasurer over the house, who is rebuked; he may be another man of the same name, so the verse was left out.
The parallel passages in Isaiah 36 and 37 were not cited, because the Kings verses already state the same events.
